title: With same app installed from distro and Flathub and pinned to Task Manager, Task Manager icons get confused about which one is running
line: When an app is installed both natively and as a Flatpak, each pinned launcher now shows its own windows.
explanation: Apps like Brave or Steam run under XWayland without naming their desktop file, so KWin looks for a desktop file whose StartupWMClass matches the window's WM_CLASS. The native and the Flatpak desktop files both match, and KWin always took the first one, so windows of both installs got the same desktop file and showed up under the same task manager launcher. When several desktop files match, KWin now reads the window process's systemd unit: windows in an app-flatpak-<id>-*.scope get the desktop file with that X-Flatpak id, the others get the non-Flatpak one.

commits.message:
x11window: pick the Flatpak or native desktop file the window runs from

When an app is installed both natively and as a Flatpak, both desktop
files share its StartupWMClass and the first one won for every window.
Now the window's systemd unit decides which of the two it belongs to.

BUG: 498875

media.caption: Before: both the native and the Flatpak window are grouped under the native launcher
Before: the Flatpak launcher (gamepad) stays inactive while its window is open
After: the native launcher only holds the native window
After: the Flatpak window shows under the Flatpak launcher, with its own icon
